sections.heading: Basic driving, occupant safety, preparation and vehicle control
sections.markdown:
# Basic driving, occupant safety, preparation and vehicle control

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
Adjust the driver’s seat before the vehicle begins moving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
Position the head restraint so it supports the head when leaning back. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A01
Keep the elbows slightly bent while holding the wheel and the knees slightly bent when operating a pedal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A01
The guide recommends keeping the right heel on the floor while moving the foot between accelerator and brake. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A01
Accelerate gently and seek a steady, safe speed rather than racing the engine. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A01
Check the speedometer periodically while traveling. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A01
Ease off the accelerator and apply the brake smoothly when slowing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A01
When stopped behind another vehicle, leave enough space to see the bottoms of its tires. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A01
Before entering traffic, look for pedestrians and approaching vehicles, then signal and move when safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A01
When reversing, turn and look behind instead of relying only on a rear-view mirror. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A01
Do not turn a moving vehicle’s ignition to the lock setting because steering can lock. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A01
Physical driving skill concerns coordinating the body with vehicle controls. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A01
Social driving skill concerns interactions with other road users. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A01
Mental driving skill includes continuing decisions and awareness of other drivers’ actions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A02
The guide recommends engine maintenance, correct tire inflation and the recommended oil grade for efficient driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A02
Removing unnecessary load, combining errands and avoiding needless idling are fuel-saving practices in the guide. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A02
Route choice and avoiding peak congestion can affect fuel use. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A03
Find the vehicle’s recommended tire pressure on the driver-side door-jamb label or in the owner’s manual. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A03
Oversteer means the car turns more than intended as the rear tires lose traction before the front tires. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A03
Understeer means the car turns less than intended as the front tires lose traction before the rear tires. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A03
The guide warns that abruptly braking during oversteer worsens loss of rear-tire traction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A04
The guide describes hand-to-hand steering as a push-and-pull method in which the arms do not cross over the wheel. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A04
The guide describes hand-over-hand steering for low-speed turns and parking. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R24 | anchor: A04
One-handed steering is reserved in the guide for reversing or briefly operating a control that requires reaching. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R25 | anchor: A05
A corner has an entry, an inside apex and an exit back into straight travel. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R26 | anchor: A05
Look well around a bend and plan the entry speed before reaching it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R27 | anchor: A05
Enter a bend at a conservative speed and avoid abrupt control movements. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0055]

sections.heading: Basic driving, occupant safety, preparation and vehicle control
sections.markdown:
# Basic driving, occupant safety, preparation and vehicle control

FACT_ID: sec06-R28 | anchor: A05
The guide explains that doubling cornering speed produces four times the cornering force. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R29 | anchor: A05
Use smooth steering, braking and accelerator inputs while cornering. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R30 | anchor: A06
On a wet road, slow down and increase the gap behind the vehicle ahead. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R31 | anchor: A06
Even light moisture can mix with roadway oil and grease to make the surface slippery. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R32 | anchor: A06
Warmer weather brings more people walking, cycling and riding motorcycles onto roadways. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R33 | anchor: A06
Allergy medicines may have side effects or interactions that reduce driving ability. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R34 | anchor: A06
Potholes can affect alignment, and large puddles can impair braking or contribute to hydroplaning. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R35 | anchor: A06
Never leave a child or pet waiting in a vehicle in hot weather. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R36 | anchor: A06
Inspect the vehicle and its fluid levels before a hot-weather trip. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R37 | anchor: A06
Vehicle payload capacity is the maximum combined passenger-and-cargo weight the vehicle can safely carry. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R38 | anchor: A06
Watch for construction workers, work vehicles and signs when seasonal road projects begin. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R39 | anchor: A06
Notice school zones and crosswalks when the school year begins. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R40 | anchor: A07
Wet leaves can create a slippery road surface. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R41 | anchor: A07
Avoid parking over leaf piles because heat from the catalytic converter can start a fire. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R42 | anchor: A07
Reduced daylight makes pedestrians and cyclists harder to see, including on familiar roads. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R43 | anchor: A07
Changing temperatures can alter tire pressure, so check inflation and tread. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R44 | anchor: A07
In excess water, slow down and avoid abrupt braking or steering. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R45 | anchor: A07
If the vehicle begins hydroplaning, hold a straight path and gently ease off the accelerator until tire contact returns. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R46 | anchor: A07
Headlights help others see a vehicle during rain, snow or fog. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R47 | anchor: A07
Avoid travel in severe winter conditions when possible; if travel is necessary, check brakes, wipers, defroster, lights and heater. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R48 | anchor: A07
On slippery winter roads, reduce speed and leave more following space because stopping takes longer. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R49 | anchor: A07
Remove ice and snow from the hood, roof and windows before driving. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R50 | anchor: A07
Winter tires do not make normal-speed travel on ice or snow safe. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R51 | anchor: A07
Bridges, elevated roads and shaded areas can freeze earlier and remain icy longer than nearby road surfaces. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R52 | anchor: A07
In rain, keep speed low enough for the wipers to maintain a clear view. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R53 | anchor: A07
Carry cold-weather emergency supplies such as blankets, water, food, a flashlight, an ice scraper and a first-aid kit. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R54 | anchor: A07
The guide directs a driver stranded by winter weather to remain with the vehicle. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R55 | anchor: A08
A driver must keep monitoring surrounding conditions regardless of the season. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0058]
